full_judgment: 5. To make the disposition by a pardanashin lady a valid one it must be proved that the disposition was substantially understood and it was really the mental set of the person who made it. The rule of law as indicated above is an exception to the general rule the law presumes prima facie in favour of the deeds duly executed, inasmuch as such transactions can be challenged only on the ground of fraud, coercion, undue influence, etc. or on the allegation of bad faith. The rule of section 111 of the Evidence Act, which provides that where there is a question as to the good faith of a transaction between the parties, one of whom stands to the other in a position of active confidence the burden of proving the good faith of the transaction is no the party who is in a position of active confidence. Relationship between the pardanashin woman and the person in fiduciary relationship, who is the done, raises the presumption of influence upon the pardanashin lady and the burden is upon the done to show that the act was spontaneous.
